clue.text: Moral reservations that carry very little weight

definitions.meaning: qualms of conscience that hold someone back from acting
an old apothecaries' unit weighing twenty grains, a tiny amount

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pangs of conscience and small apothecaries' weights of twenty grains each.

clue.text: Global outbreak of herpes?

definitions.note: an adjective defining a noun: the clue means the globe-shaped thing

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters things, so the letters of the disease's name break out into a new order

explanation.surface: A worldwide epidemic of a viral skin infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak of' rearranges HERPES. 'Global' is loose for a noun answer: read it as 'a global thing', a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball-shaped solid is round like the globe.

clue.text: Give up all hope of moving to another club?

definitions.meaning: to quit or to accept defeat without further struggle
a footballer joining another team signs again, a fresh signing

explanation.definitionFit: Quitting is one sense; sign again, as when a player joins another club, is the other.

clue.text: A spinner coming up to a tuber

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A bowler of spin moves up to bat beside a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'coming up' reads upward; 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler in cricket but is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The common edible tuber of the nightshade family.

clue.text: Additional insurance for fieldsman

definitions.meaning: a cricket fielding position on the off side, between cover and mid-off

explanation.definitionFit: Extra insurance protection, and in cricket a fielder placed between cover point and mid-off.

clue.text: A scoop for the water ouzel

definitions.meaning: a ladle or small vessel used to scoop up liquid
an old name for a small diving river bird

explanation.definitionFit: A ladle used for scooping shares its name with the river bird also called the water ouzel.

clue.text: Unconventional marines breaking in young horse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the marines break into the horse word, splitting it open

parts.note: a foal is a young horse
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Marines unconventionally breaking in a young horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking in' looks like horse training, but 'in' gives letters and 'breaking' alone signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual and relaxed behaviour is unconventional, not according to rule.

clue.text: Garbled report I get on a capital place in Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part gets on, above, the A
a garbled message is jumbled, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A muddled dispatch about an African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garbled' rearranges REPORT I into PRETORI; 'get on' sets it above A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is South Africa's administrative capital city.

clue.text: Unobtrusive engineers located in a Hertfordshire community

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: the single letter is located within the town name

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London
a means one, the roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Shy engineers based in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' stands for one, the roman numeral. Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire, a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy, reserved person keeps out of the limelight.

clue.text: Delay to take action when the tea is brewed

indicators.note: tea that is brewed is stewed and stirred, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone holds off acting until the pot of tea has brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' shuffles the ten letters of THE TEA IS; 'when' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause before doing something is to waver or delay in taking action.

clue.text: Pretend to have influence on events

definitions.meaning: to put on a show of a feeling or manner one lacks
to change or act upon how things turn out

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to feign a manner and to bring about a change in something.

clue.text: Conservative politician suited to the work he is doing

definitions.meaning: a politician of the right wing is a man of the right

definitions.text: suited to the work he is doing
definitions.meaning: the idiom for the ideal person for a particular job

explanation.definitionFit: A right-winger is a man of the right, and the ideal person for a job is said to be exactly that.

clue.text: Men who shoot back with grim enthusiasm

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for the gunners is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
dour means stern and grim

explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the crossword's usual stand-in for gunners; 'back' turns it round, and 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion and fervour are synonyms of eager enthusiasm.

clue.text: Type of 4 that's brought to book?

definitions.text: Type of 4 that's brought to book?

parts.words: Type of 4 that's brought to book?
parts.note: entry 4 ends in a word for a wrapper; this kind of wrapper is put round a hardback

explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to book' usually means called to account; here it is literal, a protective paper sleeve put on a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose paper wrapper on a hardback is a kind of protective sleeve.

clue.text: Variety of pitch?

parts.note: read not as a kind of sports ground but as a change in the musical pitch or tone of a voice

explanation.definitionFit: In music and speech, varying the tone or key is the technical term for altering pitch.

clue.text: Sitting through feature on George the First

parts.note: per means by way of, through
the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: the First, like a king's numeral, asks for the initial of the name

explanation.surface: Seated through a portrait of King George I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the First' takes the G from George, as a king's numeral would; 'on' just links in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird resting on a branch is seated there, as one sits on a high stool.

clue.text: A barman to recommend?

definitions.meaning: a lawyer called to the bar, a barrister, not one who serves drinks
to speak publicly in favour of

explanation.definitionFit: A pleading lawyer, a member of the bar, and to back or champion a course of action.

clue.text: Involved in a quest for relics of a bygone age

indicators.note: involved means intricate and tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in a search for historic relics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges IN A QUEST; 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Old collectable objects are relics of earlier times.

clue.text: Frenzied heathen god we read about in Hardy's novels

definitions.text: we read about in Hardy's novels

indicators.note: a frenzied thing is wild and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild pagan deity turns up in Thomas Hardy's fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenzied' rearranges HEATHEN GOD. Thomas Hardy set The Return of the Native and other novels on this fictional Wessex moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: This brooding moor is the imagined setting of several Thomas Hardy novels in his Wessex.

clue.text: Fair game for the ringer?

parts.note: not legitimate prey but a fairground game played by tossing rings over prizes

explanation.definitionFit: At a funfair, players throw rings to land over prizes in this stall game.

clue.text: By no means a big shot

definitions.text: By no means a big shot

parts.words: By no means a big shot
parts.note: not an important person but literally a tiny piece of ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: A small ball of lead shot fired from an air gun is the opposite of a large projectile.

clue.text: Difficult fellow who enjoys a drink in Kentucky?

indicators.note: the drinker is placed within the state abbreviation

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
someone not teetotal, NOT TT, the two T's of the abbreviation sharing the T of the last

explanation.surface: A tricky character who likes his bourbon in Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: A drinker is 'not TT' (not teetotal); the setter lets the T of NOT and the first T of TT run together, one letter doing for both.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is a hard, tangled one.

clue.text: An Asian labourer that is not very friendly to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with places the unfriendly word at the start, ahead of the abbreviation

parts.note: cool means distant and unwelcoming
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An Asian worker who is rather standoffish at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a dated and now offensive term for an unskilled Asian worker; 'to begin with' sets the unfriendly word first.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a historical word for a hired unskilled worker in Asia, now regarded as a slur.

clue.text: Early 17th-century girl bestriding a sturdy horse

indicators.note: the girl's name sits astride the other pieces, with its letters on both sides of them

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name
a cob is a short-legged, stocky horse

explanation.surface: A girl sits astride a stocky horse in the early 1600s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bestriding' pictures the girl's name with a leg on each side of the horse, as a rider sits astride.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the reign of James I of England, 1603 to 1625.

clue.text: Fabulous victim of soaring ambition

parts.note: fabulous means from a fable: the Greek youth who flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he flew too high on wings of feathers and wax, which melted and dropped him into the sea.

clue.text: A minister who does a lot of flying

definitions.text: A minister who does a lot of flying

parts.words: A minister who does a lot of flying
parts.note: a minister of religion, nicknamed as if he steered aircraft through the heavens

explanation.definitionFit: This is slang for a clergyman, especially a forces chaplain, one who guides souls toward heaven.

clue.text: Sticky matter: for corrupt advice it takes the palm

definitions.text: for corrupt advice it takes the palm
definitions.meaning: the idiom of oiling someone's palm means bribing them

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a thick lubricant and, in the phrase about the palm, the bribe paid for crooked favours.

clue.text: Furtive sort of hat style

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to sort out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hat worn in a sneaky sort of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneaky and secretive behaviour is furtive.
